multipleChoice.question: What does James tell his children at the beginning of the chapter?
options: Only listen to the word carefully
Not only listen to the word, but do it and guard it in your heart
Go immediately to the field and sow
Keep the commandment written in scripture
multipleChoice.explanation: James says: 'Do not only hear the word, but do it and guard it in your heart. For the one who hears and does not do has no fruit.'

multipleChoice.question: Who is like the wise man in Jesus's parable, according to Jesus?
options: The one who only hears the words
The one who asks questions about the kingdom
Everyone who hears the words and does them
The one who sows on the rock
multipleChoice.explanation: Jesus said: 'Everyone who hears my words and does them is like a wise man who dug deep and laid the foundation on the rock.'

multipleChoice.question: On what did the wise man lay the foundation of his house?
options: On sand
On rock
On the earth of the field
On the stones of the river
multipleChoice.explanation: The wise man dug deep and laid the foundation on the rock. When rain came and rivers beat against the house, it did not fall.

multipleChoice.question: What happens to the house built on sand when rain and rivers come?
options: It stands firm like the house on rock
It sinks slowly into the ground
It falls immediately, and its ruin is great
It is protected by the strong foundation
multipleChoice.explanation: The foolish man built his house on sand without a foundation. When rain came and rivers beat against it, the house fell immediately and its ruin was great.

multipleChoice.question: Who identifies the rain as tribulation?
options: James
Martha
Peter
Mary Magdalene
multipleChoice.explanation: Mary Magdalene says: 'Now I understood — the rain is tribulation.'

multipleChoice.question: Why does James say the Lord speaks about houses, seeds, and fields?
options: Because everyone in the village is a farmer
Because the life of the farmer shows the truth of the kingdom of heaven
Because the children need to learn how to farm
Because the Lord was a farmer himself
multipleChoice.explanation: James explains: 'Because the life of the farmer shows the truth of the kingdom of heaven. The works of the field speak about the kingdom.'

multipleChoice.question: What does Peter complain about when James gives out the seed?
options: His seed bag is too heavy
James gave Matthew much seed but him only little
The field is too far away to sow in
The sun is too hot to work in the field
multipleChoice.explanation: Peter says: 'Father, you gave Matthew much seed, but me little; give me more!'

multipleChoice.question: According to Jesus's parable of the growing seed, how does the seed sprout and grow?
options: Because the farmer waters it every day
Because the farmer works night and day in the field
By itself, while the man sleeps, and the man does not know how
Because God tells the farmer exactly what to do
multipleChoice.explanation: The seed sprouts and grows as the man does not know how. The earth bears fruit by itself, first the stalk, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.

multipleChoice.question: What does James say about the word of God in the heart?
options: It grows only if the person works very hard
It is now small but it grows, and the person does not see it
It disappears quickly if not read every day
It becomes strong only in times of suffering
multipleChoice.explanation: James says: 'We throw the seed and sleep; God makes it grow. Thus also the word in your heart: now it is small, but it grows, and you do not see it.'

multipleChoice.question: To what does Jesus compare the kingdom of God in the mustard seed parable?
options: A large tree that is immediately great
A mustard seed, smallest of all seeds, that grows into the greatest plant
A farmer who works the largest field
A seed that only grows in rocky ground
multipleChoice.explanation: Jesus says the kingdom of God is like a mustard seed — smallest of all seeds — which when sown grows up and becomes greater than all vegetables, making large branches.

multipleChoice.question: What do the birds of the sky do in the mustard tree?
options: They eat the fruit of the tree
They attack the tree and break the branches
They nest in the shade of its branches
They fly away when people approach
multipleChoice.explanation: Jesus says the mustard seed grows so large that the birds of the sky can nest in the shade of its branches.

multipleChoice.question: When were the weeds sown among the wheat in the parable of the weeds?
options: During the harvest time
While the people were sleeping
When the servants were working in the field
At the beginning of the planting season
multipleChoice.explanation: The parable says: 'While the people were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat and went away.'

multipleChoice.question: Why does the master tell his servants NOT to pull out the weeds immediately?
options: Because the weeds are too deeply rooted
Because the servants are too few and too weak
Lest in pulling out the weeds they also pull out the wheat
Because weeds can become wheat over time
multipleChoice.explanation: The master says: 'No — lest in casting out the weeds you cast out the wheat along with them. Let both grow until the harvest.'

multipleChoice.question: In James's explanation of the weeds parable, who is the enemy who sowed the weeds?
options: A wicked servant
A jealous neighbor
The devil
Death itself
multipleChoice.explanation: James explains: 'The enemy who sowed them is the devil.' The field is the world; the son of man sows the good seed.

multipleChoice.question: What does James say the righteous will do in the kingdom of the Father?
options: They will rule over all the earth
They will shine like the sun
They will harvest the wheat forever
They will teach all the nations
multipleChoice.explanation: James says the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.

trueFalse.statement: The one who hears the word but does not do it has no fruit.
trueFalse.explanation: James says: 'The one who hears and does not do has no fruit.' He urges not just hearing but doing and guarding the word in the heart.

trueFalse.statement: The foolish man built his house on the rock but without a foundation.
trueFalse.explanation: The foolish man built his house on sand without a foundation. The wise man built on the rock.

trueFalse.statement: The house built on the rock did not fall when the rain came and the rivers beat against it.
trueFalse.explanation: Jesus says that when rain came and rivers beat against the house built on rock, it did not fall — because it was founded on the rock.

trueFalse.statement: Matthew answers Peter's question about the wise man by saying the wise man was wise.
trueFalse.explanation: When Peter asks how the wise man knew rain was coming, Matthew answers: 'Because he was wise.'

trueFalse.statement: The children remain silent after hearing the parable of the two builders.
trueFalse.explanation: After James tells the parable of the two builders, the story says: 'The children are silent.'

trueFalse.statement: The seed grows because the farmer understands and controls how it grows.
trueFalse.explanation: Jesus's parable says the seed sprouts and grows as the man does not know how. The earth bears fruit by itself. James also says: 'We throw the seed and sleep; God makes it grow.'

trueFalse.statement: James gave both Peter and Matthew good seed to sow.
trueFalse.explanation: James says: 'I gave both good seed; sow therefore.' Peter received less than Matthew, but both received good seed.

trueFalse.statement: Peter immediately sows all his seed carefully across the whole field.
trueFalse.explanation: Peter takes only one grain and places it in the ground, then sits watching the ground for a long time, asking how it grows.

trueFalse.statement: The mustard seed is the smallest of all seeds on the earth.
trueFalse.explanation: Jesus says the mustard seed is the smallest of all the seeds on the earth — yet when sown it grows and becomes greater than all vegetables.

trueFalse.statement: Matthew discovers the weeds growing in the middle of the field where the wheat was already growing.
trueFalse.explanation: Matthew goes into the middle of the field where the wheat was already growing and cries out: 'Father, behold — weeds among the wheat!'

trueFalse.statement: The master of the house tells the servants to pull out the weeds right away.
trueFalse.explanation: The master says no — let both grow until the harvest, lest pulling out the weeds also uproot the wheat.

trueFalse.statement: At harvest time, the workers are told to gather the weeds first and burn them.
trueFalse.explanation: The master says: 'At harvest time I will say to the workers: take first the weeds and throw them into the fire, then gather the wheat into my storehouse.'

trueFalse.statement: In James's explanation of the parable, the field represents the kingdom of heaven.
trueFalse.explanation: James explains that the field is the world, not the kingdom of heaven. The son of man sows good seed in the world.

trueFalse.statement: Peter says he wants to shine like the sun in the Father's kingdom.
trueFalse.explanation: At the end of the chapter, Peter says: 'I want to shine like the sun.' He is referring to what James said about the righteous shining like the sun in the Father's kingdom.

trueFalse.statement: Martha is the one who first mentions that the Lord spoke a parable about hearing and doing the word.
trueFalse.explanation: Martha, lifting cups from the table, says to James: 'The Lord also spoke a parable about this, O husband.' This prompts James to tell the two builders parable.

yesNo.question: Does the house built on sand fall when the rain comes and the rivers beat against it?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. The rain came and the rivers beat against the house on sand, and it fell immediately, and its ruin was great.

yesNo.question: Does Peter ask James to give him more seed than Matthew gave him?
yesNo.explanation: Peter asks James (his father) for more seed — not Matthew. He says James gave Matthew much seed but him only little.

yesNo.question: Does the seed grow by itself in Jesus's parable, without the farmer knowing how?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. The man throws the seed, sleeps and rises, and the seed sprouts and grows as he does not know how. The earth bears fruit by itself.

yesNo.question: Is the wise man in the parable the one who only heard but did not do?
yesNo.explanation: No. The wise man is the one who both heard and did the words of Jesus. It is the foolish man who hears and does not do.

yesNo.question: Does James confirm that their own house is built on rock?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. When Peter asks 'Is our house on rock?', James says: 'Yes, on rock — for my father himself laid these stones.'

yesNo.question: Does the mustard seed become greater than all other vegetables when it grows?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. Jesus says the mustard seed, when sown, grows up and becomes greater than all the vegetables and makes large branches.

yesNo.question: Does the master of the house want to remove the weeds immediately once they are discovered?
yesNo.explanation: No. The master says to let both grow until the harvest, lest pulling out the weeds also uproot the wheat.

yesNo.question: Is the one who sows the good seed in the parable of the weeds the son of man?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. James explains that the one who sows the good seed is the son of man.

yesNo.question: Will the righteous shine like the moon in the kingdom of the Father?
yesNo.explanation: No. James says the righteous will shine like the sun — not the moon — in the kingdom of their Father.

yesNo.question: Does Matthew ask whether the word of God growing in the heart is like the mustard seed parable?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. After James explains about the word growing in the heart, Matthew asks: 'Like the parable of the mustard seed?' and James confirms: 'Certainly.'

yesNo.question: Does Matthew laugh when Peter complains about receiving less seed?
yesNo.explanation: Yes. Matthew laughs and says: 'He gave me much because I am older than you.'
